title: Diuretics: Site of Action and Electrolyte Effects
subject: Pharmacology
preview: Loop diuretics inhibit NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb and can increase urinary calcium excretion.
quickRevision: Loop diuretics inhibit NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb and can increase urinary calcium excretion.
Potassium-sparing diuretics act in the collecting system by antagonizing aldosterone or blocking ENaC.
Monitor sodium, potassium, kidney function and volume status because adverse effects differ by class.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Loop diuretics inhibit NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb and can increase urinary calcium excretion.
Thiazides inhibit NCC in the distal convoluted tubule and reduce urinary calcium excretion.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Potassium-sparing diuretics act in the collecting system by antagonizing aldosterone or blocking ENaC.
Monitor sodium, potassium, kidney function and volume status because adverse effects differ by class.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not assume all diuretic groups have the same effects on calcium or potassium.
